prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1447; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a side impact at an intersection. Claimant reports a back strain and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will route through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of impact. The driver is named on the policy and coverage was in force on the loss date.

Entry 3: Obtained statements from two independent witnesses and photos from the scene. Both witnesses describe the collision the same way the claimant and the other driver did.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, whose account matches the claimant's on the sequence of events at the intersection. No discrepancies found in the core facts.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle photos. The damage is largely consistent with the described side impact and the points of contact line up with the reported angle.

Entry 6: Requested prior claims history and repair records for the vehicle. Nothing shows earlier damage to the same areas, and no prior loss has been filed on this unit.

Entry 7: Medical records received from the initial treating facility. The back strain diagnosis fits the kind and force of the crash, and no earlier injury to that body area appears in the file.

Entry 8: Claimant's counsel provided a follow-up letter with a few additional details about the moments after impact. The core account has not changed from the first statement.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a typical course, with care tapering as the claimant improved. Latest therapy notes describe steady progress and reduced reported pain.

Entry 10: Reviewed all materials to date. Nothing in the file suggests the damage or injury predates the policy's effective date. File remains open pending final medical billing from the provider.
